title: propose().explain() dependency screen silently drops numeric fields not recommended gaussian/poisson; quickstart's strongest planted dependence never reported
reproduction: venv=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; from a dir outside any checkout run: import numpy as np; from mixle.utils.automatic import analyze_structure; rng=np.random.RandomState(0); n=240; c=rng.choice(['paid','free'],size=n,p=[.4,.6]); a=np.where(c=='paid',rng.normal(2,.5,n),rng.normal(.5,.3,n)); f=np.where(c=='paid',rng.random(n)<.9,rng.random(n)<.05); p=analyze_structure(list(zip(map(float,a),c.tolist(),f.tolist()))); print([(h.left,h.right,h.bic_gain_bits) for h in p.pairwise_hints], p.pairwise_pairs_checked). Control: replace a by np.where(c=='paid',rng.normal(2,1,n),rng.normal(0,1,n)). Script: reviews-081/pass-10/probe_deps_control.py
expected: the category<->amount pair (MI ~0.97 bits, the strongest planted dependence) is screened and reported alongside category<->flag
observed: only ((1,),(2,)) reported, pairwise_pairs_checked=1, field (0,) encoded=None because its recommendation is 'mixture'/'generalized_gaussian' not in ('gaussian','poisson'); control data (recommendation gaussian) reports all three pairs incl. (0,1) 0.38 bits; quickstart_example.py prints only 'dependency: $[1] <-> $[2]' on the shipped seed and seeds +100/+200/+300
notes: The frontier's structured candidate still models the dependence (held-out -1.43 vs -2.60), so the returned model is right; the explanation text is incomplete exactly where the dependence is strongest. The profile even warns field 0 'looks multimodal' — the bimodality is the dependence it declines to test.

title: LDAEstimator raises LDAConvergenceError (alpha fixed-point budget exhausted at residual ~1e-8) on 9 of 12 sampling seeds of the shipped LDA example
reproduction: venv python, outside any checkout: from collections import Counter; import mixle.stats as S; from mixle.inference import optimize; true=[{0:.6,1:.25,2:.1,3:.05},{0:.05,1:.1,2:.25,3:.6}]; gen=S.LDADistribution([S.CategoricalDistribution(t) for t in true],alpha=[1.0,1.0],len_dist=S.CategoricalDistribution({14:1.0})); docs=[sorted(Counter(u).items()) for u in gen.sampler(seed=3).sample(400)]; optimize(docs,S.LDAEstimator([S.CategoricalEstimator() for _ in range(2)]),max_its=60,out=None). Sweep script: reviews-081/pass-10/attacks/lda_crash.py. Also: copy the example, change gen.sampler(seed=1) to seed=3 (or sample(300) at seed 1) and run it.
expected: a fitted LDA model (optionally with a convergence warning), as for seed 1
observed: mixle.stats.latent.lda.LDAConvergenceError: lda_alpha_fixed_point did not converge after 1000/1000 iterations (iteration_budget_exhausted; residual=5.32e-08); crashes for seeds 3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11 (residuals 1e-8..1.2e-7), passes for 1,2,12; also crashes at seed 1 with 300 docs (residual 1.09e-8); seed-offset copies of the example exit 1 for +200 and +300
notes: Guard overreach: relative |dalpha|/sum(alpha) ~1e-8 at alpha_threshold=1e-8 means alpha is known to ~8 digits yet the entire EM fit is discarded. fixed_alpha= / alpha_threshold= workarounds exist but the iteration_budget_exhausted message does not mention them (only the alpha_diverging branch does).

title: mixture_reduction_benchmark's EM-refit baseline is a single fixed-seed restart stuck at a degenerate optimum; printed '5.09x closed-form tighter' conclusion is an init artifact
surface: examples/mixture_reduction_benchmark.py; mixle.ops.project (fixed rng seed, target params unused)
reproduction: Run the example (prints EM-refit KL 0.5417/0.5421/0.5435 for M=2/4/6 vs closed-form 0.5153/0.1202/0.0573). Then, venv python from the work dir: copy random_gmm/mean_log_density/kl_to_teacher from the example; teacher=random_gmm(12,2,seed=1); eval_x=list(teacher.sampler(99).sample(5000)); tlp=mean_log_density(teacher,eval_x); for seed in range(6): em=project(teacher,random_gmm(4,2,seed=7).estimator(),n_samples=4000,seed=seed,max_its=300); print(kl_to_teacher(teacher,em,eval_x,tlp)). Scripts: attacks/reduction_attack.py, attacks/reduction_attack2.py, attacks/em_monotone.py
expected: an M-component EM refit that at least does not get worse with more components, so the two columns can be 'read together' as the docstring instructs
observed: M=4 EM KL by project seed 0..5: 0.542, 0.544, 0.102, 0.377, 0.542, 0.104 (closed-form 0.120); M=8: 0.215, 0.066, 0.068, 0.514, 0.070, 0.384 (closed-form 0.023). Seed 0 (the example's) has weights [0.024,0.895,0.017,0.063] after one EM step and never leaves; 50/500/2000 iterations and any target_seed give identical 0.5420. EM warm-started from the closed-form M=4 solution improves monotonically -19414 -> -19345 in 8 its to KL 0.104.
notes: project() calls fit(data, estimator, rng=RandomState(seed)) using only the target's family; the script's 'fresh target GMM' is never used as an init. The benchmark's own takeaway sentence inverts the real picture (closed-form is a strong init; EM refines it).

title: dump_models/load_models cannot round-trip HierarchicalMixtureDistribution or JointMixtureDistribution although serialization_schema_manifest.json registers both as codec 'constructor-validated'
reproduction: venv python outside any checkout: from mixle.stats import *; from mixle.stats import dump_models; t=[CategoricalDistribution({'a':.5,'b':.25,'c':.25}),CategoricalDistribution({'a':.25,'b':.5,'c':.25}),CategoricalDistribution({'a':.25,'b':.25,'c':.5})]; hd=HierarchicalMixtureDistribution(t,[.25]*4,[[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[.3,.4,.3]],len_dist=CategoricalDistribution({8:.1,9:.2,10:.7})); dump_models(hd). And: d11=CompositeDistribution([CategoricalDistribution({'a':1.0,'b':0.0}),GaussianDistribution(-6,1)]); d12=CompositeDistribution([CategoricalDistribution({'a':0.0,'b':1.0}),GaussianDistribution(0,1)]); d21=SequenceDistribution(CompositeDistribution([GaussianDistribution(-6,1),GammaDistribution(1,3)]),PoissonDistribution(3)); d22=SequenceDistribution(CompositeDistribution([GaussianDistribution(0,1),GammaDistribution(3,3)]),PoissonDistribution(3)); dump_models(JointMixtureDistribution([d11,d12],[d21,d22],joint_weights=[[.5,.1],[.1,.3]])). Scripts: attacks/json_roundtrip.py, attacks/serial_probe.py
expected: JSON text that load_models reads back to an equivalent model (as 12 other families from these examples do, max |dlogp| <= 2e-15), or the gap disclosed in the CHANGELOG/manifest
observed: SerializationError for both, fitted or generating: HierarchicalMixture 'registered class ... requires a class-owned __pysp_setstate__ hook; constructor fields are absent: mixture_weights, topic_weights'; JointMixture 'constructor rejected serialized state'. to_json() alone succeeds (write-only). pickle round-trips both exactly. CHANGELOG discloses the gap only for mixle.stats.directional and mixle.stats.matrix; the manifest lists both classes with codec constructor-validated, state_version 1, stability provisional.
notes: These are the models of two shipped examples (hierarchical_mixture_example.py, joint_mixture_example.py). dump_models(verify=True) at least refuses loudly rather than emitting unreadable text.

title: model_comparison_example prints B's parameters/'loglik' from an MCMC chain with bulk ESS ~3 on the scale parameters and surfaces no diagnostic
surface: examples/model_comparison_example.py; mixle.ppl Mix(...).fit(how='mcmc') point summary (.dist) and summary()
reproduction: venv python outside any checkout: import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import Mix, Normal, free; rng=np.random.RandomState(0); y=np.concatenate([rng.normal(-6,1,300),rng.normal(6,1,300)]); b=Mix([Normal(free,free),Normal(free,free)]).fit(y,how='mcmc',draws=1200,burn=600,rng=np.random.RandomState(2)); print(b.dist); print(b.summary()); sum(b.dist.log_density(v) for v in y). Compare with rng seeds 3 and 4, and with the EM MLE: from mixle.inference import optimize; from mixle.stats import *; optimize(y,MixtureEstimator([GaussianEstimator(),GaussianEstimator()]),max_its=500,out=None). Scripts: attacks/modelcmp_attack.py, attacks/modelcmp_diag2.py; seed-offset copy attacks/seeds/model_comparison_example_s200.py
expected: a converged chain (or a printed ESS/R-hat warning) behind the printed 'B's fitted component means', sigma, and loglik/aic/bic row
observed: shipped seed: dist sigma2 1.616/1.746 (truth 1.0), means -5.85/5.72 (cluster sample means -5.97/5.86), loglik -1304.71 vs EM MLE -1267.32; summary(): ess_bulk comp0.arg1=3.27, comp1.arg1=2.78, ess_tail~10, sigma q97.5=4.7, acceptance 0.23. Seeds 3/4: sigma2~1.0, loglik -1267.4. Data seed +200: B means -5.39/5.47, loglik -1419.6 (~150 nats below MLE), khat 0.29. Winner (B by 567 elpd) unaffected.
notes: The example labels the column 'loglik' next to aic/bic, which reads as a fitted maximum; the ppl exposes ess_bulk/ess_tail via summary() but the example never prints them.
